answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 20 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. The island multiplier is published, charged in velvet, and ember lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 2804 identities would post 2400 proofs and burn roughly 51 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
